steps.what: Capture maintenance test results, material usage and repairs against the correct asset
Check maintenance record completeness and confirm exact history update
Record confirmed maintenance information in asset history without retyping

tasks.design: Configure the mobile work order in {OPS_SYSTEM} so the technician captures and checks maintenance data once. The confirmed record updates asset history without another transcription; missing fields and offline conflicts return to the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Field records and maintenance history may require separate entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing maintenance systems support mobile work orders and repair history.
tasks.still_hard: Accurate readings, material identification and truthful descriptions of work actually completed.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising an implausible test result and explaining repair circumstances.
tasks.altitude: Less copying where duplicate entry exists; technical decisions and release authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Identify recurring valve faults from verified history
reach.learn: Asset hierarchy and failure coding limitations

evidence.claim: Ultimo supports preventive maintenance and repair history, including mobile work-order use described in the digest; this supports native configuration, not the proposed local saving.

assumptions: Boundary is maintenance documentation after physical testing and repair, excluding repair execution, operational release and installation-only meter records. A roll-up assigns any overlapping record once.

The technician produces actual maintenance observations during unchanged physical work before s1. In s1 the technician captures asset ID, work-order ID, date, test name, reading, unit, test conditions, material code, quantity and repair description. Capture time is fully counted, not assumed to be telemetry.

In s2 the technician checks those fields and confirms the exact update version and target asset. Missing codes, conflicting identifiers or offline sync errors require manual correction; no fault code is inferred automatically.
Test native mobile forms and work-order closure before custom integration. Savings require actual duplicate entry today; existing system runtime earns none.
Allow 8 focal hours per 100 baseline for form upkeep, failed-sync handling and history checks. No free planner transcription is assumed.
National employee consultation and access requirements must be checked for timestamped mobile work orders.
unknowns: Local access and employee consultation requirements
research_questions: Does single capture reduce documentation time after offline recovery and asset-history reconciliation?

already_counted.description: Completeness checking and exact update confirmation remain counted

incremental.description: Maintain fields and handle sync failures and history audits

approvals.approved_version: Confirmed maintenance record snapshot, asset ID and target work order; any changed field or target voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=65; gross saving 35 less 8 upkeep gives net 27. Range 5-18 assumes duplicate maintenance-history entry exists, with significant offline and incomplete-record exceptions; already integrated sites gain zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record meter readings and installation data

steps.what: Read the meter and capture installation data on the field order
Verify meter readings, units and installation identity before updating the order
Enter verified meter readings and installation data into the service order

tasks.design: Use the field-order form in {OPS_SYSTEM} to capture readings and installation data once at the meter. The technician checks the display and installation identity before the confirmed snapshot updates the order; billing and return-to-service decisions are outside the automation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper meter cards may be transcribed into a separate service order.
tasks.enabler_now: Mobile work-order systems can retain entered field data as the order record.
tasks.still_hard: Reading the correct register, matching the actual meter and handling unreadable displays.
tasks.human_edge: Physical confirmation of which device and register were observed.
tasks.altitude: The technician may avoid a second entry but still performs and verifies the field observation.

reach.task: Resolve meter identity exceptions before downstream processing
reach.learn: Register types, units and asset matching

evidence.claim: OutSmart provides digital work orders for installers; this supports considering existing field-order configuration, without proving meter-reading automation or a local labour gain.

assumptions: Boundary is recording an installation's meter data, excluding physical installation, billing and maintenance repair history. Any record shared with the maintenance task is assigned once in a roll-up.

The technician produces the installation observations through unchanged field work before s1 and captures site ID, service-order ID, meter serial, register ID, observed reading, unit, timestamp, installation status and relevant installation details in s1. All capture time stays counted.

The technician verifies the exact record against the physical device in s2. A missing serial, uncertain reading or ambiguous register requires manual resolution; no structured address, reading feed or automatic device recognition is assumed.
Test native mobile order configuration before any custom link. Handheld entry already integrated with the service record gives no additional saving.
Allow 6 focal hours per 100 baseline for form maintenance and failed-sync correction; no administrator is expected to absorb new transcription for free.
Check national consultation and permissions for mobile records and timestamps.
unknowns: Whether current handheld entry already updates the order
research_questions: How much second-entry time remains after current handheld tools, and does single capture survive offline work without rework?

already_counted.description: Physical reading and field-data capture remain counted
Device identity, units and reading verification remain counted

incremental.description: Maintain forms and correct sync or mapping failures

approvals.approved_version: Exact verified meter record with meter serial, register, reading, unit and service-order target; any change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=85; gross saving 15 less 6 upkeep gives net 9. Range 1-5 assumes paper-to-order duplication remains but unreadable displays and connectivity require manual work; already integrated handheld entry gains zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Shut off service and notify repair crews

steps.what: Assess major repair requirements and establish safe service isolation arrangements
Shut off service and verify the required isolation under site procedure
Notify repair crews of major repairs and communicate the verified isolation state

tasks.design: Retain site assessment, physical shutoff and direct crew notification. Existing {TELEPHONY} supports the handover, but the technician confirms isolation and obtains acknowledgement under site procedure.
tasks.previous_blocker: The physical condition and required isolation cannot be inferred safely from a notification rule.
tasks.enabler_now: No supported change removes the assessment or field action.
tasks.still_hard: Unexpected energy sources, site access and communicating an accurate isolation state.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising unsafe conditions and verifying the physical result.
tasks.altitude: The technician's safety responsibilities and service authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Give a clear isolation handover before major repair work
reach.learn: Site-specific isolation boundaries and acknowledgement procedure

evidence.claim: Assessment, physical isolation and an acknowledged repair handover remain human work in this scenario.

assumptions: Boundary starts with a field condition requiring evaluation and ends with crew notification; excavation, pipe replacement and re-energisation are outside this task.
The technician observes the field condition in s1 and establishes the actual isolation state in s2 before describing it in s3. Crew acknowledgement is produced during s3, not assumed in advance.
Site safety procedures and authorised roles already exist; this design does not generate new isolation instructions or override required permits.
Test existing communication and work-order configuration for a separate administrative problem before custom tools; no software change is proposed here.
Zero incremental upkeep because physical practice and communication are unchanged.
research_questions: Does current procedure require additional authorised personnel before shutoff, and how is that effort allocated?

already_counted.description: Assessment, shutoff verification and crew communication remain fully counted

incremental.description: No changed system or procedure to maintain

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net saving 0. Major-repair isolation and acknowledged crew notification are retained without inventing a removable reporting baseline.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Report hazardous field situations and damaged meters

steps.what: Identify hazardous field situations and damaged or missing meters without unsafe investigation
Report the hazardous situation or meter discrepancy and confirm receipt

tasks.design: The technician reports the actual observation directly through {TELEPHONY} and confirms the responsible person's receipt. A system does not decide that a location is safe or that a meter is stolen from an incomplete report.
tasks.previous_blocker: Hazard significance and uncertain meter identity require field context.
tasks.enabler_now: No evidenced change removes the reporting conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Urgency, poor location information and distinguishing missing equipment from an incorrect asset record.
tasks.human_edge: Communicating uncertainty and responding to follow-up questions without delaying urgent escalation.
tasks.altitude: The technician continues to observe and report; investigation and response decisions stay with authorised roles.

reach.task: Provide precise initial information for hazard response triage
reach.learn: Escalation routes and distinction between observation and confirmed cause

evidence.claim: A direct hazard report with explicit uncertainty and receipt confirmation remains substantive communication work.

assumptions: Boundary is identifying and reporting the field situation, excluding repair execution, isolation accounted elsewhere and the supervisor's incident investigation.

The technician produces the observation in s1 and conveys known location, meter identity where readable, observed condition and urgency in s2. Clarification and acknowledgement time are counted; no ready discrepancy code or structured address is assumed.
Existing asset records supply only an expected meter location, not proof of absence; uncertainty remains explicit.
Consider native mobile reporting only if a separate duplicate-entry baseline is demonstrated. No custom model or workflow is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new tool, classifier or reporting requirement is introduced.
unknowns: Urgent reporting channels and acknowledgement arrangements
research_questions: Which report delays arise from reaching the responsible person rather than drafting or data entry?

already_counted.description: Observation, report and receipt confirmation remain fully counted

incremental.description: No new tool or workflow to maintain

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net saving 0. The scenario keeps direct reporting and clarification for uncertain field hazards and meter discrepancies.
